title: Qwen3.8 on DGX Spark (GB10): SGLang + DFlash2 spec-decode stack
config_notes: One-command boot-persistent SGLang install with five switchable targets, pinned image digest + checkpoint revisions, systemd, OpenAI/Anthropic-compatible API on :30000 and a keepalive proxy on :30001 for agent CLIs. Hardened against the GB10 unified-memory trap: Docker caps --memory 100g plus --mem-fraction-static 0.50 (0.70 for the 1M-context mode), --disable-flashinfer-autotune for boot-to-boot determinism, --sleep-on-idle. 27B uses DFlash2 block-diffusion speculative decoding (draft block 8); Flash-Next 176B is served on ONE box by mmap-ing the 51B N-gram/PLE table from NVMe through the page cache (torch.from_file + madvise(MADV_RANDOM), 48 GB backing file) with the model's own NEXTN/MTP head as draft, --max-running-requests 1, --max-total-tokens pinned to 190000, and a proxy prompt ceiling of 128K tokens. FP8 targets add --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3; 1M mode patches YaRN (factor 4.0) into both target and draft config.json.

title: MLX-Flash: MoE expert caching / SSD streaming on Apple Silicon
model: Qwen3-30B-A3B (4-bit), Qwen1.5-MoE-14B, Qwen3-8B, Qwen3.5-27B, Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, Qwen3.5-397B
config_notes: Runs models larger than RAM on Apple Silicon by streaming cold MoE experts from SSD and keeping predicted-hot experts in RAM (97% routing prediction), reading macOS kernel vm_statistics64 every inference call (0.1 ms) to shrink/expand cache under pressure, madvise(MADV_FREE) page-cache control, 7-tier mixed precision (hot experts FP16/Q8, cold Q2), and shared-expert pinning for Qwen MoE. Server mode is a Rust sidecar on :8080 routing to N Python workers with session affinity (warm KV), exposing OpenAI + Ollama + MCP APIs; auto-profiling picks DFlash / LayerSkip / EAGLE-3 speculative strategy by AR speed (>50 tok/s = skip). Also StreamingLLM sinks and 4-bit quantized KV for 4x longer context.

title: Qwen3.6-27B on a single RTX 4090: llama.cpp recipes and per-category quality receipts
config_notes: Recommends mainline llama.cpp (built with -DGGML_CUDA=ON, CUDA 12.8) over ik_llama.cpp, because mainline implements SSM_CONV_TREE and can load Qwen3.5-4B (vocab 248,320, identical BPE and specials) as a true same-vocab speculative draft with no token-translation layer; ik_llama 4274 cross-vocab spec-dec hits higher peak tps but silently corrupts JSON braces, list separators and tool-call boundaries. Working configs: 8K ctx with q8 KV (C1-agg) and 32K with q4 KV on both target and draft (C1-32K-dkv, required because same-vocab spec-dec hangs >32K with q8 KV). title: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next 176B on a single DGX Spark via vLLM + mmap'd n-gram table
model: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (~176B: 125B main + 51B n-gram, 6B active), RadixArk NVFP4 checkpoint
config_notes: The 122 GiB NVFP4 checkpoint cannot coexist with a usable KV cache in 128 GB unified memory, so the repo patches the official vLLM image (vllm/vllm-openai:qwen38-flash-next) to mmap the 44-48 GiB n-gram 'PLE' embedding shards from NVMe and gather the ~16 rows x 160 bytes each token needs, dropping resident weights to ~76 GiB; PREWARM=1 streams the table once at boot. It also fixes two GB10 bugs: a vLLM block_size overwrite that made every prefix-cache hit restore an all-zero Mamba state (PREFIX_CACHE=1 now default), and the non-deterministic QSA persistent_topk kernel, replaced by a compiled deterministic kernel (DET_TOPK=1) with EXACT_TOPK=1 as a slower fallback. MODE=hybrid converts the dense GDN/QSA/shared-expert side layers to blockwise fp8-e4m3 (prepare-hybrid.sh) while experts stay NVFP4. Serve knobs: GPU_MEM=0.80 (0.85 drifts to swap, 0.875 OOM-killed on a 300k prefill), MTP=2 speculative tokens, SEQS=8 (benchmarking at 1-2 flatlines aggregate tok/s on silent queueing), CTX=262144 native or 500000 with YARN=1, KV_DTYPE=fp8_e4m3 for 1.9x KV / 1M context at a quality cost, PAD_M4=1 for the blockwise-fp8 GEMM when prefix caching is off.

title: Qwen3.8-27B on SGLang for DGX Spark: three speculative engines, measured flag stack
config_notes: Opinionated start.sh / start-dspark.sh / start-dflash.sh wrappers over the cookbook-pinned lmsysorg/sglang:qwen38-27b image (and the digest-pinned dev-qwen38-27b-dflash2 tag), with three swap-in speculative modes: EAGLE/MTP 3/1/4, native DSpark block-7, and DFlash2 block-8 with the pinned z-lab/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2 block-diffusion drafter. Flags diverge from the SGLang cookbook where measured on-device: GDN bf16 (cookbook float32 cost -3%), mamba-radix-cache-strategy extra_buffer_lazy, --mem-fraction-static 0.90 (0.95 for MTP), chunked prefill 8192 (cookbook 2048), torch.compile + decode graphs, --num-continuous-decode-steps 2, FP8 KV e4m3, and --cpuset-cpus 5-9,15-19 pinning the container to GB10's ten 3.9 GHz Cortex-X5 cores so the scheduler/tokenizer never land on the 2.8 GHz A725s. GDN state pool sized as --max-mamba-cache-size = concurrency x 4; YaRN to 1M context works on the MTP path only (the override leaks into DSpark/DFlash2 draft configs and crashes at boot). bench/ndec.py does two-call net-decode A/B and bench/ab-image.sh interleaves sides inside one session because two boots of the same image differed 6.5% on the essay probe.

title: Qwen3.8-27B NVFP4 on SGLang (DGX Spark / SM121): click-run profiles + matched evals
model: Qwen3.8-27B NVFP4 (r0b0tlab/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4-MTP-sm121) with z-lab/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2 (K8), RadixArk/Qwen3.8-27B-DSpark (K7) or in-checkpoint EAGLE/MTP 3/1/4

title: vllm-mlx: continuous-batching OpenAI/Anthropic server for Apple Silicon (Qwen3 MoE)
config_notes: A vLLM-style server on native MLX (mlx-lm / mlx-vlm / mlx-audio / mlx-embeddings) that adds what bare mlx-lm lacks: continuous batching, paged KV cache, trie-based prefix caching shared across requests, and an SSD-tiered KV cache (--ssd-cache-dir) for long-context agents, exposing both OpenAI /v1/* and Anthropic /v1/messages from one process. Qwen-specific recipe knobs: --reasoning-parser qwen3 to surface thinking as reasoning_content, --moe-top-k expert reduction (+7-16% on Qwen3-30B-A3B), --mtp speculative decoding for Qwen3-Next, --spec-prefill attention-based sparse prefill for TTFT, --warm-prompts to preload popular prefixes at startup (1.3-2.25x TTFT), and 19 MCP tool-call parsers including Qwen. Ships its own bench-serve harness (--workload, --repetitions, CSV/JSON/SQLite output) and model inspect/acquire/convert commands.

title: Qwen3.5-122B-A10B on DGX Spark: 28.3 -> 52 tok/s vLLM optimization stack
model: Qwen3.5-122B-A10B (Intel/Qwen3.5-122B-A10B-int4-AutoRound + Qwen FP8 donor); same stack on Qwen3.5-35B-A3B
config_notes: Five independent, additive optimizations on a single GB10 (ASUS Ascent GX10, 273 GB/s LPDDR5x), all baked into ./install.sh and Dockerfile.v2: --attention-backend FLASHINFER (vLLM defaults to FLASH_ATTN on SM121), a rebuilt hybrid INT4+FP8 checkpoint where the 144 shared_expert dense tensors come from Qwen's FP8 release while routed experts stay INT4 Marlin, add-mtp-weights.py registering the 785 MTP tensors that Intel AutoRound ships in model_extra_tensors.safetensors but omits from the index (--speculative-config {"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":2}), and a runtime INT8 LM-head Triton GEMV patch (per-channel BF16->INT8 at first request, single kernel launch reading the 729 MB head once per batch, ~84% of memory bandwidth vs ~24% for the BF16 matmul) plus @triton.autotune and a cherry-pick of vLLM PR #38325 swapAB SM120 FP8 GEMM. Serve flags: --max-model-len 262144, --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 (0.85 if OOM), --reasoning-parser qwen3, tool parser qwen3_xml for Qwen3.5. --enable-prefix-caching is deliberately omitted (DeltaNet hybrid attention on vLLM 0.19); an optional TurboQuant KV variant trades -22% speed for 4x KV capacity. Extensive 'graveyard' section: NVFP4 RedHatAI 16.6 tok/s, FP8 KV negligible, EAGLE-3 loses to MTP-2, SERE expert re-routing 0%, abliterated BF16 variant needs 244 GB and OOMs.

title: Qwen3.5-122B-A10B on a DGX Spark with DFlash block-diffusion speculative decode
model: Qwen3.5-122B-A10B (bleysg/Qwen3.5-122B-A10B-int4-fp8-hybrid; Intel AutoRound INT4 for dflash/base/mtp profiles) + z-lab/Qwen3.5-122B-A10B-DFlash drafter
config_notes: One-shot curl|bash installer that pulls a prebuilt sm121 vLLM 0.23 image and a ready-to-run hybrid INT4+FP8 checkpoint, then applies five runtime patches in-place (sentinel-guarded, vLLM unmodified on disk): a scale-block KV-cache unify so the hybrid GDN+mamba target absorbs the drafter's attention spec, an align-aware resolve_kv_cache_block_sizes that uses the GCD hash block size 2240 so prefix caching coexists with DFlash, an INCConfig.maybe_update_config hook dispatching Fp8LinearMethod for shared_expert, a batched int8 w8a16 Triton GEMV lm-head that keeps the bf16 weight for the shared drafter, and an FLA sm121 99 KiB shared-memory gate lift. Defaults tuned for one user with up to 3 concurrent streams: --gpu-mem 0.82 (0.88+ over-subscribes and swaps, hard-freezing the host), --ctx 262144, --max-num-seqs 3, --max-batched-tokens 8192, --load-format fastsafetensors, --tool-call-parser qwen3_xml (hermes returns 200 with empty tool_calls), --reasoning-parser qwen3. Four profiles: dense (default, hybrid + int8 lm-head + DFlash n=12), dflash (largest KV pool), base (no spec), mtp (native head). Documents an 'amortization law': the dense levers are worth +28% at accept length 1, +10% at ~6.4 and ~0% at ~8.3 because speculative verify amortizes the always-on weight reads.

title: Qwen3.8 Flash-Next: 8-slot concurrent serving on a 128 GB Mac via oMLX
config_notes: Measured recipe for one oMLX 0.6.4 process (an MLX serving runtime, not stock mlx-lm) advertising max_concurrent_requests=8 on a 128 GB M5 Max-class MacBook Pro: 2 orchestrators sized toward 252K + 2 TDD toward 32K + 2 coders and 2 auditors toward 64K. The decisive setting is scheduler.chunked_prefill=true with prefill_priority 'context' and decode_fairness=true, plus server.burst_decode_mode 'balanced' and a memory guard (prefill_memory_guard, memory_guard_tier balanced, soft_threshold 0.85, hard_threshold 0.95) because the real budget line is the ~107.5 GB Metal working-set cap, not 128 GB RAM. Per-model settings: mtp_enabled=false (measured 60.9 tok/s solo with MTP on vs ~86 off on this box/checkpoint), max_context_window=262144, and qwen4_ple_ssd_offload=true so the n-gram table is SSD-mapped; launch with --paged-ssd-cache-dir ~/.omlx/ssd-cache. Operating rules are all measured traps: salt every repeated benchmark prompt (identical fillers hit the prefix cache and walls collapse 12.1 s -> 3.4 s), read memory with /usr/bin/footprint not RSS, stop by port because omlx serve spawns a surviving child, and never cold-fill both 252K orchestrators while the fleet is resident. Raw JSON receipts ship in results/; every mlx-serve comparison is labelled 'receipt pending re-run'.

title: qwen38-flash-next-mlx: MLX runtime and streaming quantization for Qwen3.8-Flash-Next
model: Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (125B-A6B hybrid Gated-DeltaNet / Qwen-Sparse-Attention MoE, model_type qwen4_exp) - published MLX 8bit / 6bit / mixed-4_8bit / 4bit builds
config_notes: The qwen4_exp architecture is carried by no released mlx-lm or mlx-vlm, so this repo ships a corrected version of ml-explore/mlx-lm PR #1788 as qwen4_exp.py (bundled as model_file in every published checkpoint, loadable through stock mlx-lm with trust_remote_code=True). The three fixes are correctness-critical, not speed: RMSNorm must be x/rms*(1+w) with w zero-initialised (the PR's x/rms*w sign-flips half the channels of every residual-stream read), the n-gram hash seed must be 1234 (the PR's seed 0 makes every bigram/trigram lookup hit an unrelated row of the 51B table), and sparse-attention prefill must mask per-query over its own visible prefix ANDed with causal (the PR leaks the global tail to all queries past 2048), plus an exact l2norm for DeltaNet q/k. Quantization is streamed shard by shard so the 360 GB bf16 release never has to sit next to its own quantized copy: routed experts (120.8B, 96.6% of the model) at --bits group 64, the 128 n-gram shards at --ngram-bits group 32 because 160 is not a multiple of 64 and unquantized the tables alone are 102 GB, everything else at --other-bits, and the MoE router, shared_expert_gate, residual write gates, DeltaNet in_proj_a/b and indexer projection kept in bfloat16; the 4B MTP head is dropped.

claimed.context: wikitext-2 (test) perplexity of the upstream bfloat16 model, teacher-forced over 145 windows of 2048 tokens
perplexity of the recommended mixed-4_8bit build (106.2 GB), +0.0128 NLL/token vs bf16 [95% CI +0.0109, +0.0148], 128/145 windows worse = +1.3%
uniform 4-bit build (103.8 GB), +0.1872 NLL/token [95% CI +0.1778, +0.1968], 145/145 windows worse = +20.6% cost

title: Running Qwen3.5-35B-A3B and Qwen3-Coder-Next locally on 32-64 GB Apple Silicon MacBooks
model: Qwen3.5-35B-A3B (35B MoE, 3B active, unsloth GGUF Q4_K_M / ollama qwen3.5:35b-a3b); also Qwen3-Coder-Next 80B MoE and Qwen2.5-Coder-32B
hardware: other: Apple Silicon MacBook with 32 GB or 64 GB unified memory (M1/M2/M3/M4)
config_notes: Decision-tree runbook with a check-compatibility.sh probe and a RAM auto-detecting start-llama-server.sh, covering both llama-server (brew install llama.cpp, Metal by default) and the simpler Ollama path (ollama pull qwen3.5:35b-a3b, OpenAI-compatible API on :11434). The 32 GB recipe is llama-server -hf unsloth/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-GGUF:Q4_K_M --ctx-size 32768 --n-gpu-layers 99 --no-mmap --flash-attn on --temp 1.0 --top-p 0.95 --top-k 40 --min-p 0.01 --jinja --port 8080; the 64 GB recipe swaps in Qwen3-Coder-Next Q4_K_M at --ctx-size 65536. Two non-obvious points: --ctx-size must be capped because the model's default 256K context OOMs instantly, and --no-mmap loads the model fully into RAM upfront to avoid page-fault stuttering on macOS. The aggressive Q2_K Coder-Next build deliberately drops to --n-gpu-layers 40 to prevent swap storms on first run (tune to 60-80 once stable), and if a 32 GB box swaps the guide's order is reduce ctx to 16384, then GPU layers to 30, then close apps, and avoid conversation branching because llama.cpp handles linear conversations better. Ships ready-made agent configs: .aider.model.metadata.json (registers context windows so Aider stops warning), .aider.model.settings.yml (num_ctx), opencode.jsonc with both llama.cpp and Ollama providers, setup-pi-local.sh writing ~/.pi/agent/models.json, and setup-llm-local.sh for Simon Willison's llm CLI.
